sources: SSC Combined Graduate Level Examination 2025 notification: https://ssc.gov.in/api/attachment/uploads/masterData/NoticeBoards/Notice_of_adv_cgl_2025.pdf
SSC notices on ssc.gov.in (notice board and candidate login)

admitCard.where: Your candidate account on ssc.gov.in and the SSC regional website for your region
admitCard.when: A fresh admission certificate applies to each stage; the published 2026 Tier 1 window has ended. Follow the official notice for the timing of any later stage.
steps: Sign in to your candidate account on ssc.gov.in with your registration number and password, or open the admit card link of your regional SSC website.
Download the exam city intimation slip first and confirm your city and date; it is not the admit card.
Download the admit card when your region publishes it and take a clear printout.
Check name, photograph, roll number, shift, reporting time and centre address against your application, and write to your regional office at once if something is wrong.
Keep every stage's admit card safe: SSC releases a fresh one for each tier and you need it again at document verification.
carry: The original photo ID named in the admit card instructions (Aadhaar, PAN, passport, driving licence or voter ID)
Only what the admit card allows: phones, smartwatches, calculators and study material are not allowed inside
admitCard.note: **The published Tier 1 window, 30 September–30 October 2026, is over.** As of the 2 November review, a new CGL 2026 answer-key/result notice was not verified on SSC’s board. Check [SSC](https://ssc.gov.in/) for the actual release, challenge period and fee. Use the [shift archive](/exam-analysis/ssc-cgl-2026/) as unofficial reporting and keep Tier 2 preparation moving; no confirmed Tier 2 date is supplied here.

answerKey.summary: As checked on 2 November, a CGL 2026 tentative-key/response-sheet release was not verified on SSC’s notice board. When SSC publishes it, read the exact viewing and challenge period in that notice. The final result and normalised marks are separate from a personal raw-score estimate.
steps: When SSC publishes the matching CGL 2026 key notice, open its official candidate link and follow that notice’s login instructions.
Save the available response sheet and key, and estimate your raw score using the applicable marking scheme. Normalised result marks are separate.
For a representation, follow the notice’s exact question-selection, evidence, fee, payment and submission instructions within the specified window.
Keep the payment/submission acknowledgement and follow the subsequent final-key and result notices.
answerKey.fee: The charge and payment conditions must be read in the actual CGL 2026 answer-key notice when published; this page does not carry forward a previous cycle’s fee.
answerKey.note: No confirmed answer-key day or Tier 2 date is supplied here. Save any response sheet and acknowledgement while the official access window is available.

result.summary: Results are published as PDF lists of roll numbers with category-wise cutoffs on ssc.gov.in, and individual marks are released separately through the candidate login after each stage's result.

stages.what: A qualifying screen for Tier 2. The result comes with category-wise cutoffs, and marks follow through the candidate login. Tier 1 marks are not counted in the final merit.

Paper 1 decides the merit out of 390 marks (normalised across shifts), with section-wise qualifying minimums; the Computer Knowledge module and DEST are qualifying only. JSO candidates additionally sit Paper 2 (Statistics).

The final result leads to the First Round of Tentative Allocation under SSC's sliding mechanism. Post preferences are collected through an online option form on ssc.gov.in before the result, and candidates who do not submit preferences are not considered for any post.
Conducted by the user departments after the final result, with originals and photocopies of age, educational and category documents. SSC maintains no wait list for this examination.

result.scorecard: After each stage's result, SSC opens a marks link on ssc.gov.in where candidates sign in and download their marks and the cutoff details; the link stays open for a limited period, so save a copy.
